whatItIs.text: A staple baked from flour and water, usually leavened with yeast, and one of the oldest prepared foods there is.

historyNote.text: The oldest known bread, from a 14,500-year-old Natufian site in Jordan, predates farming; leavened loaves appear in records by about 6000 BC in Mesopotamia, and Egypt later refined yeast-raised bread.

howToChoose.text: Look for a loaf with a little weight and a fresh smell; skip crushed or hollow-feeling packaging if you want it to last past today.

storage.text: Keep at room temperature wrapped, or freeze what you will not finish; the fridge actually speeds staling.

useItUp.text: Stale bread is a feature: croutons, breadcrumbs, panzanella, French toast or a buttery bread pudding.

substitutions.note: for breadcrumbs in coatings and meatballs; drier, so season less
